'''Ethel Marian Scott''' (born July 1956)<ref>{{cite web|title=Ethel Marian SCOTT|url=https://beta.companieshouse.gov.uk/officers/OJloT--qX-yiE7M0os-5PZtJB94/appointments|website=Companies House|access-date=19 February 2018}}</ref> is a Scottish statistician, author and academic, specialising in [[environmental statistics]] and [[statistical modelling]]. She is [[Professor (highest academic rank)|Professor]] of Environmental Statistics at the [[University of Glasgow]].<ref name="Scot Sci">{{cite web|title=Professor Marian Scott OBE, FRSE, FISI, CStats|url=http://www.scottishscience.org.uk/members/professor-marian-scott-obe-frse-fisi-cstats|website=Scottish Science|publisher=Scottish Science Advisory Council|access-date=19 February 2018}}</ref><ref name="bio Glasgow">{{cite web|title= Prof E Marian Scott|url=https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/mathematicsstatistics/staff/escott/|website=School of Mathematics & Statistics|publisher=University of Glasgow|access-date=19 February 2018}}</ref> She is additionally vice-president (International) of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Professor Marian Scott: Teaming up with China in the appliance of science can only benefit Scotland|url=https://www.scotsman.com/news/opinion/professor-marian-scott-teaming-up-with-china-in-the-appliance-of-science-can-only-benefit-scotland-1-4576539|access-date=19 February 2018|work=[[The Scotsman]]|date=4 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Council & Committees|url=https://www.rse.org.uk/about-us/our-governance/council/|website=The Royal Society of Edinburgh|access-date=19 February 2018|date=2016-07-26}}</ref> and a member of the [[Scottish Science Advisory Council]].<ref name="story">{{cite web|title=Marian Scott|url=http://www.universitystory.gla.ac.uk/biography/?id=WH1892&type=P|website=The University of Glasgow Story|publisher=University of Glasgow|access-date=19 February 2018|date=17 March 2010}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Scott has a degree in statistics and a PhD from the [[University of Glasgow]]. Her thesis was on the sources of error in [[radiocarbon dating]], and was supervised by Murdoch Baxter and Tom Aitchison.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stats.gla.ac.uk/~marian/|title=index|website=www.stats.gla.ac.uk|access-date=2019-06-26}}</ref>

Her research interests include model uncertainty and sensitivity analysis, modelling how pollutants disperse in the environment, radiocarbon dating and assessing [[animal welfare]].  

In 2005, Scott was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]] (FRSE), Scotland's [[national academy]] of science and letters.<ref name="FRSE">{{cite web|title=Fellows – Professor Ethel Marian Scott OBE FRSE|url=https://www.rse.org.uk/fellow/marian-scott/|website=The Royal Society of Edinburgh|access-date=19 February 2018|date=2017-05-19}}</ref> In the [[2009 Queen's Birthday Honours]], she was appointed an [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) for services to social science.<ref name="LG">{{London Gazette |issue= 59090 |date= 13 June 2009 |page= 12 |supp= y }}</ref>

Professor Scott was awarded the [[Royal Statistical Society]] Barnett Award in 2019<ref>{{cite web|title=The Barnett Award|url=https://rss.org.uk/training-events/events/honours/the-barnett-award/|website=The Royal Statistical Society|access-date=30 November 2020|date=2020-11-30}}</ref> for "her outstanding, pioneering research into the application of innovative statistical techniques to environmental issues."
